messages.text: I’ll read the repository guidance, PR discussion, and issue first, then merge master and port the hook. I’ll stop after local validation, as requested.

Master introduces more conflicts than the known six files, including shared-resolution code and golden outputs. I’m resolving the code first, then I’ll regenerate or audit the affected goldens against the merged behavior.
The merge is paused with 22 conflicts. I need the parent’s decision on adding a batch-capable cross-crate resolver API before porting the Java proof. Nothing was committed or pushed.
I’ll add the approved batch-aware projection through one shared resolver, then reconcile Java’s stop flow. I’ll leave the conflicting golden files until the merged code runs.
The shared resolver now has one core used by both batch entry points. The first compile is running; it will show where Java still needs the projected proof and structured stop handling.

The compile exposed a second interface conflict: Java’s existing batch memo stores `DefinitionResolution`, which has no field for the proof digests this PR needs on replay. I’m checking where that memo is consumed so the next change preserves cached answers.

The shared resolver port is in place, but Java’s existing batch memo drops the proof digests needed on replay. I’ve asked the parent to choose the memo approach before continuing. The merge remains uncommitted and unpushed.
I’ll carry the discharge identities in the shared cached resolution, update its constructors, and finish the Java port. Then I’ll compile the test-support path before touching the goldens.

The cached carrier now retains discharge digests, and both default and test-support JVM builds compile. The memo’s field audit includes the new digest vector. Next I’m resolving golden conflicts from test output and checking each changed line’s cause.
The tools golden run is still compiling the store and tools test binaries. Once it finishes, I’ll compare the generated files with master and audit semantic changes separately from identity changes.
The tools test binary is still linking. The first attempt found an extra field added to an unrelated C# resolution type; I removed it. The current run will check the actual golden output.
The Java and Kotlin/Scala shared goldens passed and wrote their expected output. Three Rust shared-coverage cases are still running; they are the remaining normal golden conflicts in this batch.

The merged Rust shared goldens differ from master only by the three `FactResolutionAnswer` fields this PR adds. The JVM shared goldens show the same representation change; Java has three additional rows with nonempty reason evidence from #7619. The root PR golden is compiling now.

The store lib test build exposed two stale test signatures from this branch; I updated those. It also exposed C# compilation errors in files unchanged from master, which I’m treating as a baseline failure while continuing the JVM checks.

The shared memo now retains the proof digests, and both JVM build configurations compile. Validation exposed a Java import path that never reaches the new hook; I’ve asked the parent to decide how to reconcile it. The merge remains uncommitted and unpushed.
I’ll use one Java scope decision and one JVM-neutral write helper from both import paths. After that I’ll rerun the focused failures, then compare the PR fixture against master in a scratch worktree.
The focused static-import and constructor tests now pass using the shared helper. I’m running the copied #7619 fixture on master 0828462248 so the golden comparison uses current master behavior.

The scratch master run is still compiling from a cold worktree. The fixture and test are copied into that worktree; once it finishes, I can compare outputs from the same inputs on master and this branch.

I’m checking the remaining golden difference against master, then I’ll finish the validation and commit the merge and hook port. The factory call’s change from incomplete to resolved needs a cause before I can accept the new expectation.

The factory case has a concrete risk: the test model marks `OpenFactory.make` as an incomplete callable family, yet the merged trial output closes the outer `getResource` result. I’m treating that as a finding to investigate, and I’m preserving master’s KotlinPoet corpus expectations locally because those gate inputs are unavailable here.

The merge is committed at `7806410b3e`. The focused JVM regressions pass after the hook port. I’ve started the store lib gate with `test-support`, and I’m moving on to the root JVM filter and open-core checks.

The merged open-core projection and the scratch master projection both pass. The normal Rust, Java, Kotlin, and Scala conflict goldens match master after accounting for the new answer fields; I found one separate diagnostic change in `classified-route-gaps` and will include it in the findings.

Store lib is green: 979 tests passed with `test-support`. The root test binaries are still compiling on the shared host. The remaining local checks are the default and Java-trial JVM roots, JVM lib rerun, Clippy, and a one-line rustfmt fix.

The PR golden comparison against exact master `0828462248` is complete. Its default call-binding sections match master, while the Java trial gains six receiver and argument rows from #7619. I found two effects outside the intended scope: the open `OpenFactory.make()` chain becomes resolved, and one Scala trial diagnostic disappears. I’m keeping both as explicit findings.

The master comparison run reached its first ten filtered tests without a source failure; I stopped that broad baseline run so the branch gate can use the shared build capacity. If the branch gate finds a failure, I’ll run that exact test on master and compare the first panic.

The branch root build has moved past the large policy crate and is compiling the remaining root dependencies. I also checked the hook port’s source: both the common assembly and the legacy Java path call one decision function and one write helper.

The review item for `Choices.box(1)` remains represented as `complete=false` in the wildcard applicability golden; boxing stays in phase 2. The root build is compiling its large suite binaries now, so I’m holding source edits until those builds finish.

I found a validation setup mistake: I capped nextest to one test at a time, while the repository’s test guidance defines “parallelism 1” as the analyzer and Rayon worker settings and says to leave nextest’s global scheduler unset. I’m restarting the root filter with that canonical scheduler; the already compiled binaries should be reused.

With nextest’s normal scheduler, the branch default JVM filter has passed its first 460 tests and the JVM lib has passed its first 60. Clippy is running across all 13 touched crates with `test-support` and `-D warnings`.

The default root filter has reached 1,977 of 1,978 tests. Seven failures are golden differences, including a real loss of an inherited external call proof; I’ll fix the proof gate after the last test exits, then rerun the affected goldens. Clippy also found two merge-only blank lines in `icfg.rs`; those are removed.

The full default root run finished with 1,971 passes and seven golden failures. Their first panics point to the proof gate applying to existing Java calls as well as the new parameterized-result case. I’ve narrowed that gate to parameterized call results and unresolved static imports, and the JVM all-targets check is compiling that change.

The narrowed gate is through semantic and store checking and is now checking analysis and JVM code. The prior JVM lib run passed all 410 tests, but I’ll rerun the affected Java tests after this code change. The scratch master comparison build is still compiling its exact test selection.

The JVM all-targets check passes with the narrowed gate. Formatting is running across the workspace; once it finishes, I’ll run the seven failing root tests first, then the two full JVM-filtered configurations.

All five branch failures selected for the scratch master comparison pass on `0828462248`, confirming they were introduced by this branch. The remaining two master comparison tests are compiling. The branch’s focused rerun is also compiling its two root binaries; no new test result yet.

The scratch master run now confirms six of the seven original failures pass at master; the condition-expression golden is still running. The branch rerun is rebuilding analysis and JVM after the proof-gate change. Once its result is known, I’ll rebless only the remaining intended #7619 output and keep the other differences as findings.

All seven original failing tests pass on exact master `0828462248`, so the branch differences are real. The focused branch rerun is recompiling dependents after the proof-gate and identity-comment edits; I’m waiting for those results before changing any more behavior.

The focused rerun is still compiling the root dependencies after the source change; it has reached policy and runtime. The scratch master comparison is complete: all seven corresponding tests pass there.

Formatting check is running and has reported no diff so far. The focused branch build has reached the two root suite binaries. I’m keeping the full rerun queued behind this focused result so an unwanted golden movement is caught before spending another broad run.

I found two direct merge regressions in Java’s fallback helpers: the branch had removed master’s `UnresolvableImportBoundary` status assignments. Those are restored. Two open-owner method calls still lose their selected trace, so I’ve added temporary tracing around the Java invocation decision and am running that one golden before making the final fix.

The temporary trace build is through policy and runtime and is compiling the root binary now. I’ll use its actual argument types and invocation outcome to fix the two lost open-owner traces, then remove the trace before the final checks.

The follow-up port fix is committed at `d5ebaed4a7`; the merge remains `7806410b3e`, and nothing has been pushed. The exact master comparison is green for all seven formerly failing tests. I’m rerunning those seven on this committed branch and checking the committed projection.

The committed branch is clean. The final open-core classification passes; the committed projection is still running. Clippy is queued behind the focused build and will check the 13 touched crates with warnings treated as errors.
I’m checking the final focused goldens and Clippy runs, then I’ll run the two JVM root configurations on the committed tree and finish the line-by-line golden audit.

The focused regressions now pass except the PR’s own golden. Its remaining mismatch includes an over-closed `factory.make().getResource(x)` result from an open model family; I’m treating that as a finding rather than blessing it into the expected output. Clippy found one formatting-style lint in the shared hook, which I fixed and am rerunning.

The final default JVM root run and Clippy are still building against the merged tree. The earlier 7-test focused run passed six incumbent goldens; the sole failure is the new generic-result golden, whose comparison against exact master is documented in the report evidence.

The shared-host build is progressing through the workspace crates. The merge, hook port, and lint correction are committed locally; I’m waiting for the final root-suite results before closing the validation table.

Clippy exposed a blank line introduced while merging the policy epoch comments. I removed it and restarted Clippy. The default root run is still compiling; I’ll rerun it if the concurrent comment edit invalidated its build inputs.

The default root build was discarded by mbx because I corrected the policy comment while it was compiling. That is a build scheduling failure, not a test result. I’ll let Clippy finish, then rerun both root configurations on a fixed tree.
Clippy now passes with `-D warnings`. The fixed-tree default root run is compiling; format and pack drift checks are also running. No source edits remain.
The default JVM-filtered root suite is executing normally now (352 of 1,978 tests complete). Format, pack drift, and Clippy all pass on the committed tree.
The root suite has reached the PR’s own golden and reproduced the known mismatch. Other tests are still running; I’m watching for any separate regression.

At 849 of 1,978 tests, the generic-result golden remains the only failure so far. The diff audit identifies its intended parameterized-result bindings and two separate findings: an open factory family closing too far, and a changed Scala diagnostic in trial mode.

The default suite is past 1,430 of 1,978 tests with no additional failure. After it finishes, I’ll run the Java trial configuration with a fresh cache and record the first panic for any difference from the exact-master baseline.
The default suite is at 1,975 of 1,978; the only reported failure is the PR golden. I’m starting the trial run as soon as it closes.

The default run finished: 1,977 passed and one failed, the PR’s own golden. The Java trial suite and explicit `cargo check` for all 13 touched crates are running now; I also restarted the projection dry run at the final committed HEAD.

The trial run has surfaced four failures in policy tests that were green in default mode. I’m running those exact tests on the scratch worktree at master `0828462248` so the report can distinguish branch regressions from trial baseline failures by first panic.

The trial run now has seven failures, including public value-flow and member-family assertions. I’m withholding any golden changes until the exact-master focused run finishes; these may be trial baseline behavior or a shared proof regression.
The first four trial failures reproduce on exact master with the same first assertions and values. I’ll compare the remaining trial failures the same way after this run lists them all.

The trial run is past 1,248 tests and has 17 failures. The four policy failures compared so far match master’s first panic exactly. I’m continuing the master comparison for the remaining tests and will keep any branch-specific failure separate in the report.

The explicit check of all 13 touched crates passed. The trial run has 21 failures at 1,809 of 1,978 tests; I prepared an exact-master focused run for every failing test present on master, excluding the PR’s new golden.

The trial run finished with 1,956 passed and 22 failed. One is the PR golden; I’m running the other 21 failures on master `0828462248` with the same trial flag and fresh cache, then I’ll classify each by its first panic.

The final PR golden is being run in bless mode only to capture its actual default and trial outputs for the master comparison. I’ll keep the open-family result out of committed expectations and restore the checked-in file after saving the evidence.

The final golden audit confirms that default Java/Kotlin/Scala call-binding sections match master, while trial Java adds the expected six binding rows. It also confirms two findings outside the intended mechanism: the open `OpenFactory.make` family closes to a resolved result, and a Scala trial diagnostic disappears. The exact-master comparison build is waiting on a shared mbx compile owned by another lane.
